memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Outside the curtain that shields the ark of the covenant law in the
tent of meeting, Aaron is to tend the lamps before the LORD from
evening till morning, continually. This is to be a lasting ordinance
for the generations to come'" - Lev 24:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron's task was to tend the lamps from evening till morning. Through
the dark hours, while the camp slept, someone was awake keeping the
light alive before God.

There is comfort in that picture. The nights in the wilderness were
long and the desert dark, but inside the tent of meeting a light was
always burning, always attended.

Dear reader, you may be in a night season right now. Perhaps the
diagnosis has not changed, the job has not come, the relationship has
not healed. Nights are long when you are the one lying awake.

Hold on to this: God does not sleep. The psalmist says He who watches
over Israel will neither slumber nor sleep (Ps 121:4). The light before
Him is not left unattended, and neither are you.

Notice also that the lamp burned just outside the curtain — as close to
God's presence as the priest could come. Your night is not being lived
far from God. It is being lived near Him, even when it does not feel
that way.

Jesus said, I am the light of the world; whoever follows me will never
walk in darkness (John 8:12). The light is tended. Morning does come.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "night season" am I walking through at present?
2. Do I believe God is awake and attentive while I struggle?
3. Who could I sit with in their night this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You neither slumber nor sleep. Keep my faith
burning through this night season, and let me trust that morning will
come. Amen.
